entities.summary: William de La Mare was an English Franciscan theologian who played a significant role in the medieval intellectual landscape. Born in England, de La Mare spent most of his life in the Holy Land, where he taught at the University of Beirut and debated with fellow scholars from the Muslim world. His writings on theology and philosophy influenced a generation of thinkers, including the famous theologian and statesman, Thomas Bradwardine. De La Mare's legacy extends to the present day, with his works still studied by scholars and theologians. In 1290, de La Mare died in the Holy Land, leaving behind a body of work that continues to shape our understanding of medieval thought. This legacy is a testament to the enduring power of intellectual curiosity and the importance of fostering dialogue between cultures.
